name: filing_sim
hypothesis: Firms that rewrite much of their 10-K vs last year's (low similarity) earn lower future returns: managers change disclosures when news (often bad) arrives, investors rarely compare filings side by side, so prices adjust slowly over months. For ASAM (long-only): a screen of stocks to avoid.
definition: Cosine similarity (word counts) between a firm's original 10-K and its most recent original 10-K filed 9-15 months earlier (WRDS bow_cossim, lookback 1-4, amendments skipped). Low = changer. Monthly value = latest with published_date <= month-end, at most 15 months old.
source: WRDS SEC Analytics Suite, wrdssec.bow_cossim (Bag of Words); linked via wrdssec.wciklink_gvkey and CRSP-Compustat (ccmxpf_lnkhist)
citation: Cohen, Malloy & Nguyen (2020), Lazy Prices, Journal of Finance 75(3), 1371ff., doi:10.1111/jofi.12885
inputs_required: 10-K text similarity (cosine), SEC acceptance date and time, EDGAR filing date, CIK-gvkey link, CCM link, NYSE trading days
timing_rule: exact: SEC acceptance time (New York) at or before 4 p.m. -> same trading day; after 4 p.m. or no time -> next trading day; acceptance date after the EDGAR filing date (WRDS re-processing date, mostly 1994-2002) -> EDGAR filing date, next trading day
notes: Stocks only (panel has no ETFs; ETF rows would be n/a). Usable from 1998 (EDGAR phase-in); last filings 2024-12, so 2025 values are 2024 10-Ks. Column format_change_2010_14 flags values from 10-Ks published 2010-2014: a filing-format change tripled 10-K length; in 2010-2012 the largest firms were 57-63% of the bottom fifth (English-only cosine_eng did not fix it). Paper's sample ends 2014 -> 2015-2024 is out of sample. Process and decisions: signals/lazy_prices/progress.md.

name: net_issuance
hypothesis: Firms that shrink their split-adjusted share count (net buybacks) earn higher future returns and net issuers lower: managers sell shares when they think the stock is expensive and buy back when cheap, and investors underreact. Slow (a year or more). For ASAM (long-only): tilt toward net buyers-back; one half of the issuance + insider-cluster combination.
definition: 12-month log change in split-adjusted shares outstanding (CRSP shrout x mthcumfacshr) with a 4-month skip: ln(adj[t-4]/adj[t-16]). Positive = net issuer, negative = net buyer-back. Firm level: a firm with 2+ listed share classes gets one value for all classes, ln(sum W / sum W*exp(-x_class)) with W = class market value at t (per-class value in net_issuance_class). No value unless every month of the window has a CRSP price.
source: CRSP CIZ crsp.msf_v2 (shrout, mthcumfacshr, mthprc); timing measured with CRSP share history (crsp.stkshares) and EDGAR filing dates (wrdssec.wrds_forms)
citation: Pontiff & Woodgate (2008), Share Issuance and Cross-sectional Returns, Journal of Finance 63(2), 921-945, doi:10.1111/j.1540-6261.2008.01335.x
inputs_required: CRSP monthly shares outstanding, cumulative share-adjustment factor, price; for the checks also total return, CRSP share history, EDGAR 10-K/10-Q filing dates, CIK-gvkey and CCM links
location: data/issuance_insider/net_issuance_monthly.parquet:net_issuance (checks in the same file: net_issuance_skip3, net_issuance_skip6, net_issuance_pit, comp_issuance, net_issuance_5y; events: data/issuance_insider/net_issuance_events.parquet); shared drive
timing_rule: assumed: share counts used 4 months after their month. CRSP dates many counts at the fiscal period end, before the 10-K/10-Q is public; measured 2003-2025, a 4-month skip uses under 1% of share changes before public (1 month: 34-56%). Check net_issuance_pit uses each count's 10-K/10-Q public time (at or before 4 p.m. -> same trading day, else next) where matched.
test_results: Backtest 2026-11-16 (firm level across share classes; investable: price >= $5, me >= $250M; monthly; 1980-2025): Q5 (net buyback) beat the market +2.2%/yr VW (t 2.4), +2.8% EW (t 2.0); Q5-Q1 6.3%/yr EW (t 3.4); Fama-MacBeth with reversal, bm, size 5.6%/yr (t 3.0); FF5+UMD alpha of Q5 small (VW +0.7%, t 1.3; loads on RMW, HML, CMA); weaker 2008-2025 (Q5-Q1 VW 3.1%, t 1.1); annual December check Q5 VW +1.6%/yr vs market (t 2.2). Details: signals/issuance_insider/backtest.md.
notes: Stocks only (panel has no ETFs; ETF rows would be n/a). Primary fixed before any return test; named checks in the same file: net_issuance_skip3, net_issuance_skip6, net_issuance_pit, comp_issuance (Daniel-Titman 1-year composite issuance, counts dividends), net_issuance_5y. 88.8% of panel rows have a value (new listings need 16 months). Extremes are real (serial diluters; SPAC trust redemptions look like large buybacks - consider excluding SIC 6770). One half of the issuance_insider project with insider_cluster; combinations C1 (net shrinker and insider cluster buy) and C2 (average rank) use the two primaries only. Process and decisions: signals/issuance_insider/progress.md. Changed 2026-11-16 to firm level across share classes (per-class values let conversions look like buybacks, e.g. Berkshire A -> B); ~1% of rows affected.

name: insider_cluster
hypothesis: When several officers or directors of a firm buy its stock on the open market within a day of each other, the stock earns higher returns over the following weeks to months: insiders know more about the firm, several buying together is a stronger signal than one, and investors underreact to the Form 4 filings. Purchases only (insider sales are mostly for liquidity). For ASAM (long-only): a buy-side screen; one half of the issuance + insider-cluster combination.
definition: Number of different officers/directors whose purchase (Form 4/5 code P, acquired, common stock, original filings, filed 0-90 days after the trade) was part of a tight cluster - another officer/director of the same firm (gvkey) bought on the same or an adjacent trading day - and became public, with its partner's filing, in months t-2..t. 0 = no cluster (firm's filings visible); blank = firm not linked to SEC filings, or before 2006-03. A joint filing counts as one insider; the firm-level value goes to every permno of the gvkey.
source: SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets (Forms 3/4/5 XML as filed, quarterly 2006Q1-2025Q4, sec.gov, free); issuer CIK -> gvkey via wrdssec.wciklink_gvkey (dated link; a CIK linking to only one gvkey is used outside its dates) -> permno via CRSP-Compustat (ccmxpf_lnkhist); NYSE trading days from CRSP
citation: Kang, Kim & Wang (2018), Cluster Trading of Corporate Insiders, working paper (UNSW / UW-Milwaukee / UCF); see also Alldredge & Blank (2019), Do Insiders Cluster Trades with Colleagues? Evidence from Daily Insider Trading, Journal of Financial Research 42(2), 331-360, doi:10.1111/jfir.12172
inputs_required: Form 3/4/5 non-derivative transactions (code, acquired/disposed, trade date, shares, price, security title), filing date, form type, reporting owner and relationship, issuer CIK; CIK-gvkey link, CCM link, NYSE trading days; panel market value (check insider_buy_value_3m)
location: data/issuance_insider/insider_cluster_monthly.parquet:insider_cluster (checks in the same file: insider_buyers_1m, insider_buy_value_3m, insider_npr_6m; events: data/issuance_insider/insider_cluster_events.parquet; raw SEC pull: data/issuance_insider/sec_trans/sec_submissions/sec_owners.parquet); shared drive
timing_rule: exact: Form 4/5 filing date -> next trading day (the SEC data sets have no time of day; assumed after the close); a cluster purchase counts once its earliest partner's filing is also public; trades filed more than 90 days after the trade dropped
test_results: Backtest 2026-11-16 (investable; monthly; 2006-04 to 2025-12): no premium. Cluster portfolio vs market -2.9%/yr EW (t -1.3), -3.9% VW (t -1.6); FF5+UMD alpha -0.8% EW (t -0.5), -2.5% VW (t -1.1); Fama-MacBeth with controls -1.4%/yr (t -0.6); named checks not significant; C1 underperforms, C2 = net_issuance alone. Small caps not tested. Details: signals/issuance_insider/backtest.md.
notes: Stocks only (panel has no ETFs). Primary fixed before any return test; named checks in the same file: insider_buyers_1m (buyers made public in month t), insider_buy_value_3m (purchase dollars over 3 months / firm market value - keeps price typos up to 377,051x, use by rank only), insider_npr_6m (net purchase ratio over 6 months, insider-days). 96.9% of panel rows from 2006-06 have a value; 6.8% have a cluster (46% of purchase insider-days are clustered; Kang et al.: over 40%). Kept on purpose ('keep everything'): every code P counts, incl. IPO and offering purchases (7 of the 10 largest clusters in the stock's IPO month; 4.8% of cluster months in a stock's first 3 CRSP months) and plan-like fractional purchases; a CRSP daily price check would be a new, separately recorded version. No data before 2006 (LSEG insider data not readable on the WRDS account; library asked). Anchor sample 1986-2016, so 2017-2025 is out of sample. Combinations C1/C2 with net_issuance use the primaries only. Process and decisions: signals/issuance_insider/progress.md.
